newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech blue chips push PSE to 3rd straight advance.
newsitem.headline: Czech blue chips push PSE to 3rd straight advance.

text.p: Czech blue chips rallied on the Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday, pushing the market to its third consecutive advancing session.
SPT Telecom, CEZ, Komercni Banka, and Chemopetrol all posted gains as the PX50 index rose 4.0 points, or 0.80 percent, to break through the 500 level, closing at 503.8.
Total volume, boosted by heavy block trading in SPT, was heavier at 708,860 shares, on turnover of 1.07 billion crowns.
"Some of the prices have become very attractive and investors are sniffing around, but I still think we aren't going to see a major shift in the bourse this summer," said one local trader.
A total of 160,333 shares of SPT traded off market between 3,370.95 and 3,530 crowns.

On the broader market, Philip Morris Czech unit Tabak jumped 110 crowns to 7,751 after Wednesday's announcement that the firm was raising prices of its cigarettes by up to one crown per package, effective July 7.
Tabak controls some 80 percent of the Czech cigarette market.
Meanwhile, shares of investment fund RIF edged up one crown to 781.
On Thursday Finance Ministry fined RIF's manager, Prvni Investicni a.s.(PIAS), a record 10 million crown fine for illegal financing operations and other legal violations.
PIAS, a unit of bank IPB, is the largest Czech investment fund manager, controlling holdings through its funds of some 30 billion crowns.

The ministry said it has also ordered changes in the management of PIAS, and said it must change "its depositors for its unit trusts and investment funds", which is currently IPB. As well, PIAS must cancel its contract making IPB its broker.
But brokers said the fund got off relatively lightly, avoiding forced administration, and that RIF shares, as well as IPB shares, should be largely unaffected by the news.
